newsitem.title: KENYA: Nairobi bourse index falls for third straight day.
newsitem.headline: Nairobi bourse index falls for third straight day.

text.p: The Nairobi Stock Exchange (NSE) share index fell for a third straight day on Tuesday since the International Monetary Fund halted a key aid package, bourse officials said.
The NSE 20-share index fell 19.47 points to 3408.75 from 3428.22 at Monday's close. The NSE tumbled 24.95 on Monday.
"Brokers are idling around with nothing to do. Activity has been very minimal," said a trader.
Foreign investors made no deals at the NSE on Monday but on Tuesday a foreigner brought 15,370 shares in Kenya Commercial Bank, which closed at 91.50 shillings from 91.
Brokers said the market remained tense as investors gauged government reaction to the IMF loan cancellation last Thursday but added the overall mood was more optimistic than since the decision.
But bourse officials warned that investors remained wary of a general strike called for Friday by an opposition-backed alliance demanding constitutional reforms.
The agricultural board was quiet on Tuesday, with Rea Vipingo Plantations edging up 25 cents to close on 8.70. Sasini Tea and Coffee was unchanged at 80 shillings.
With a go-slow by air traffic controllers in its fourth day, Kenya Airways eased five cents to close at eight shillings.
A total of 2,186 shares in Nation Printers and Publishers changed hands, pushing the price up two shillings to close at 108. National Industrial Credit added 1.5 shillings to close at 53.
In the industrial sector 50,000 highly sought-after Dunlop Kenya shares traded at 560 from 270. "Dunlop shares are hardly ever seen so there was a lot of interest," said a bourse floor trader.
Kenya Power and Lighting lost five shillings to close at 165.
After a high level of bond trading on Friday and Monday as foreign investors left the market, turnover fell on Tuesday to 116 million shillings from 230.4 million.

The fourth issue of the Central Bank of Kenya floating-rate treasury bond sold at 102.6650 percent from 102.5321. The third issue of the Central Bank of Kenya floating-rate treasury bond traded at 102.5050 percent from 102.1365.
